rationale: The candidate reads coherently in all four views as one stepped compact bar/lifted mass, so it is not a fragmentation failure. The blue access edge is acknowledged only weakly: there is no strong carved entry seam, court, or undercut that materially opens the ground toward the frontage, so the public threshold is underdeveloped for neighborhood living. The silhouette is acceptable but a bit code-like in its repeated setbacks; it has more of a generic stepped mass than a meaningfully inhabited terrace section. Programmatically, the mass can plausibly support neighborhood living as a compact mixed-use object, but the ground/public-space relation is not yet strong enough for a hard fit pass. The references reinforce that the right direction is a courtyard, void, bridge, or terraced public core rather than a sealed stepped block.
